title: Selling and Promotion - Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA - Promotion: Promotional Mix
subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which element of the promotional mix involves paying for non-personal communication through mass media channels like TV or newspapers?
questions.explain: Advertising is defined as any paid, non-personal form of communication through various media formats by an identified sponsor.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Coupons, sweepstakes, free samples, and rebates are all classified under which part of the promotional mix?
questions.explain: Sales promotions are short-term incentives given to encourage the immediate purchase or sale of a product or service.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: What is a major advantage of publicity/public relations over advertising?
options: It guarantees an exact broadcast time and message control.
It allows the company to hide flaws about its products.
It is often perceived by the public as more credible and objective since it comes from a third party (like a news outlet).
It requires less creativity than creating an advertisement.
questions.explain: Because publicity is often disseminated via news channels rather than paid sponsors, consumers tend to view it as more credible and objective than traditional ads.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which element of the promotional mix is the most expensive per contact but has the highest rate of converting prospects to customers?
questions.explain: Personal selling involves face-to-face communication, making it highly persuasive and responsive, but the cost per individual interaction is very high.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: When a company emails an exclusive 15% discount code directly to its current email newsletter subscribers, what type of promotion is this?
questions.explain: Direct marketing involves sending targeted promotional messages directly to specific individuals, often via email, direct mail, or telemarketing.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A manufacturer of camping gear sets up a booth at a sporting goods trade show to convince retail buyers to stock their tents. This is an example of a:
questions.explain: A push strategy involves promoting a product to members of the distribution channel (like retailers or wholesalers) to 'push' the product onto store shelves.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A toy manufacturer creates a massive display in the front of a retail store right before the holidays. This display is best described as:
options: Point-of-purchase (POP) display (a form of Sales Promotion)
questions.explain: POP displays are physical setups in stores meant to catch the customer's attention and encourage impulse buying, acting as a sales promotion.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: A major automotive brand pays a movie studio to have its newest sports car prominently driven by the hero in a blockbuster film. This promotional tactic is known as:
questions.explain: Product placement is the integration of a product into entertainment media, like movies or TV shows, in exchange for payment.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: If a clothing retailer offers a 'Buy One, Get One 50% Off' deal for the weekend, this is an example of what type of promotion?
questions.explain: Consumer sales promotions are directed toward the final consumer to stimulate immediate sales, such as a BOGO deal.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA

questions.q: Which of the following activities falls under Public Relations?
options: A salesperson demonstrating a vacuum cleaner in a customer's home.
Sending a direct mail catalog to past customers.
Writing a press release about a company's new eco-friendly manufacturing plant.
Paying for a sponsored post on a social media platform.
questions.explain: Issuing a press release is a standard Public Relations function intended to generate free, favorable media coverage and improve the company's image.
questions.subject: Intro to Marketing Concepts FBLA
